texts.facts: 8) The Tezpur Development Authority (TDA) on 13.03.2018 issued notice to the petitioner stating that he had made illegal construction within Tezpur Master Plan Area that was brought under the Tezpur Master Plan, vide Government Notification dated 25.10.1977 and since he had started construction work without obtaining prior permission from the TDA in violation of Section13(1) of the Assam Town and Country Planning (Amendment) Act, 1959, the petitioner was asked to stop the construction work and he was asked to give reply as to why appropriate action should not be taken against him as per the provisions of Sections 30 (B) (1), 31, 51 and 52 of the said 1959 Act. Following the provisions of the Revised Master Plan and Zoning Regulation for Greater Tezpur - 2031 the TDA on 19.03.2018 issued notice to the petitioner asking him to demolish all the illegal constructions made by him for commercial purpose over Baotali land where Baotali land are used purely for cultivation purpose and that construction of building over cultivable land are not permissible without obtaining prior approval/permission from the Development Authority concerned. 10) The petitioner filed writ petition W.P.(C) No.1788/2018 praying for setting aside the Notice dated 19.03.2018 issued by the Tezpur Development Authority whereby he was directed to demolish his said illegal commercial construction made over agricultural ( Baotali) land, without any authority and without taking due approval. 11) Thereafter the petitioner filed his second writ petition W.P.(C) No.521/2023 praying for direction to the State respondents not to implement the Gazette notification relating to said Revised Master Plan and Zoning Regulation for Greater Tezpur - 2031 Notification dated 24.08.2010. 13) Considering the decisions of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the cases of Union of India -Vs- Tulsiram Patel, reported in (1985) 3 SCC 398 and CCE -Vs- Pradyumna Steel Ltd,SLP(C) No. 18531 of 1995 by the said common Order dated 19.03.2024 the Hon'ble single Judge also came to the finding that the Assam Government Notification dated 24.08.2010 covers the area of petitioner's constructions and the policy decision of the State Government in notifying the area incorporated in the Revised Master Plan and Zoning Regulation for Greater Tezpur - 2031 is not in violation of Article 14 of the Constitution. As such the Hon'ble Single Judge did not find any reason Page No.# 5/7 to interfere with impugned Notice dated 19.03.2018 issued by the Tezpur Development Authority to the petitioner asking him to demolish all the illegal constructions made by him for commercial purpose over his cultivable (Baotali) land without any authority and necessary approval from the authority concerned. 15) For the reasons above by the said common order dated 19.03.2024 the Hon'ble single Judge dismissed both the writ petitions W.P.(C) No.1788/2018 and W.P.(C) No. 521/2023 preferred by the petitioner. 16) However, by the said common order dated 19.03.2024, the Hon'ble single Judge granted liberty to the petitioner that if he within a period of one week from the date of the said order approaches the Chairman of Tezpur Development Authority for re-classification of his land in question for the purpose of allowing him to use his constructions for commercial purposes, the authority concerned would take a decision on the same immediately as per its discretion and till then the notice dated 19.03.2018 (issued by the Tezpur Development Authority to the petitioner asking him to demolish all the illegal constructions made by him for commercial purpose over his cultivable land involved in the case) shall not be acted upon till a decision is taken on the petitioner's said representation. 17) From the minutes of the District Level Committee, District-Sonitpur, Tezpur, presided by the District Commissioner & Chairman, District Level Committee (DLC), Sonitpur, Tezpur, regarding re- classification of land held on 10.07.2024 (Annexure-3 to the petition) it is seen that after considering all the facts and gravity of the matter, perusing and discussing the relevant reports, joint verification report etc., the said District Level Committee decided not to recommend Re- classification proposal of land as applied by the petitioner from Baotali to commercial/industrial Page No.#
